questions.question:
Two statements are followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true even if they do not conform to real-world knowledge, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. 

**Statements:**

1. Some cottages are huts.

2. All huts are sheds. 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some sheds are cottages.

II. No shed is a cottage.

options.text: Only conclusion II follows
Only conclusion I follows
Either conclusion I or conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
**Least Possible Venn Diagram:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f09e7ea402dd021483ccd0326d4f978d764b2e350e1fc802276ea1cbdae2fa8.png] **

Conclusions:

I. Some sheds are cottages → **Follows **(Some cottage are huts and all huts are shed than some shed will be cottage. It is definitely true)

II. No shed is a cottage → Doesn't** Follows **(Because some cottage are huts and all huts are shed than some shed are cottage. Than no shed is a cottage is not possible.Hence it does not follows)

Hence, **"only conclusion I follows".**

**Conclusions :**

I. No pomegranate is a plum.

II. No plum is a tree.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the statements is as below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ef6d4d3b8c10b073c2fd38f2f513e685c0e4525f2301468310861413be155d8.png] 

**Conclusions:**

Hence, the correct answer is "**All the conclusions follow"**.

II. Some pigeons are birds.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow.

Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow.

questions.solution:
Statements:

All pigeons are crows.

No crow is a bird.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

No soap is a dessert.

All desserts are cups.

**Conclusions:**

I. No dessert is a soap.

II. Some cups are desserts.

III. Some desserts are soaps.

IV. All cups are desserts.

options.text: Both conclusions I and IV follow.
Only conclusion I follows.
Only conclusion II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/99dcc1c27adad523cb128cb0ec84c04d93ab22d01d6fb87c2e2efed86a6c84ba.png] 

The possible Venn diagram is given below:-

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ce100023659a7e885880104ba7ee48449335842b0734eb752834b360be0121e.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No dessert is a soap. → True (No soap is a dessert, so we can say that no dessert is a soap.)

II. Some cups are desserts. → True (All desserts are cups, so we can say that some cups are desserts.)

III. Some desserts are soaps. → False (No soap is a dessert, so there is no relation developed between desserts and soaps as some desserts are soaps.)

IV. All cups are desserts. → False (All desserts are cups, but all cups can not be desserts.)

Hence, **"option 4"** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true even if they do not conform to real - world knowledge, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. 

**Statements : **

1. All towns are cities. 

2. No city is a village. 

3. Some cities are corporations. 

**Conclusions : **

I. Some corporations are villages. 

II. Some towns are corporations. 

III. No corporation is a village.

options.text: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows
Only conclusion II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements will be as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9fae24671b43941d4ce6b7615efffce50bb2d84b2bc22077019a1a3b704193ec.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. Some corporations are villages → **False** (It is possible but not definite because there is no direct relation between corporation and villages.)

II. Some towns are corporations → **False** (It is possible but not definite because there is no direct relation between towns and corporation.)

III. No corporation is village → **False** (It is possible but not definite.)

When we combining the statement I and II we can say that either I or III follows 

Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows 

Hence,** either I or III** is the correct option.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Some** and **No** is complementary pair.
 
• **Elements** in the I and III conclusion are **same**.
 
• **Individually both the statements are false.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] Hint__**

Conditions of Either-or case:

1. Individually both the conclusions should be false.

2. One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative (Complementary pair)

 
• The two complementary pairs are:

 
• All + Some not
 
• No + Some
